title: Offline-first SDK: partial-sync quickstart and proxy pattern (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working quickstart and design sketch for an "offline-first" SDK workflow that lets apps (mobile, low-connectivity web, intermittent edge devices) operate with local inference stubs and partial-sync to Redwood. Focus: minimal integration friction, predictable token usage accounting, and smooth recovery when connectivity resumes.

Context / why this exists:
- We keep getting requests from engaged customers building field/edge apps where connectivity is spotty (logistics, rural clinics, in-vehicle systems).
- Existing SDK quickstarts assume always-on connectivity and a single-authoritative endpoint which makes UX bad when disconnected.
- Goal is a lightweight pattern that can be adopted in the hosted API, Dedicated, and Private modes with small SDK surface changes.

Non-goals (for initial iteration):
- Full CRDT-based document merge engine (too big).
- On-device heavy model execution. We'll assume small local stubs and server inference for heavy ops.

High-level pattern (sketch):
1) Local store: small on-device KV (SQLite / RocksDB) holds: pending-ops queue, last-known-model-version, cached responses (prefix cache), and sync metadata (op ids, vector clock/simple timestamps).
2) Proxy sync agent: a tiny background worker that attempts to sync pending ops to Redwood endpoints when network available. It implements backoff and capability detection (can we reach dedicated pool or must go to hosted?).
3) Partial-sync model: we represent user interactions as append-only ops (typed messages: prompt, edit, feedback). Server applies ops in order; on reconnect, the client streams missing responses and reconciles.
4) Telemetry and accounting: every local op has a provisional token estimate; final token usage only recorded after server ack — SDK reports both local-estimate and server-validated counts to app and billing telemetry.

Quickstart: developer-facing steps (minimal integration)
Prereqs:
- Redwood API key with offline-sync feature flagged (dev/test keys will auto-enable).
- Mobile app with persistent storage (SQLite recommended).
- Networking hook to allow background sync tasks (iOS background fetch / Android WorkManager).

Step 0 — install:
- npm: "@redwood/sdk-offline" (experimental)
- or pip: redwood_sdk_offline (py)

Step 1 — initialize store and proxy (pseudocode):
- redwood.offline.init({storage: "sqlite", dbPath: "app://redwood.db", apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY})
- redwood.offline.startSyncAgent({intervalSec: 30, maxBackoff: 300})

Step 2 — send a user request (local-first):
- const opId = redwood.offline.enqueue({type: 'generate', model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Summarize receipt', meta: {estimated_tokens: 120}})
- UI shows a provisional state ("pending — will complete when online") using cached policy.

Step 3 — server ack and reconcile:
- When syncAgent gets a successful upload it receives: ack {opId, model_version, tokens_used, response}
- SDK writes ack into store, replaces provisional UI entry, and emits events to app (onResponse, onCostChange).

Step 4 — conflict / duplicate handling:
- If server returns a different response for same opId (rare), app receives onDivergence(opId, serverResponse, localDraft). Default: show server response and stash local draft in "edits" bucket for user review.

Implementation notes and heuristics (dev/eng):
- Op model: keep it tiny. {id, type, payload, ts, estimated_tokens, client_signature}
- Auth: use short-lived provisioning tokens for devices. SDK should support key rotation and device reproof without manual re-issue.
- Cost accounting: apps must surface both "estimated" and "final" costs; billing is based on final usage. SDK will allow showing provisional credits consumption.
- Privacy: allow an opt-out that never sends full prompts (only embeddings or meta), only used for features where PII is disallowed.
- Model selection: default to a smaller/cheaper model when offline (server may accept and then upgrade on sync).

Local proxy details (practical):
- Proxy endpoints: /v1/offline/sync (batch up to N ops per request) and /v1/offline/ping (capability check).
- Contract: server returns per-op ack with definitive token counts and the final output payload.
- Batching: group small ops to reduce TLS overhead; aggressive batching when on WiFi and device on power.

Developer API examples (conceptual):
- redwood.offline.enqueueGenerate(prompt, opts) -> returns local id + event emitter
- redwood.offline.on('response', (opId, resp) => {})
- redwood.offline.getProvisionalCost(opId)

Testing checklist (manual + automated):
- [ ] Simulate immediate-online: enqueue -> immediate ack path
- [ ] Simulate delayed-online: enqueue while airplane mode -> re-enable network -> validate sync and ack
- [ ] Network flaps: ensure idempotent uploads and de-dup by opId
- [ ] Partial-batch failure: some ops in batch fail; verify retries/backoff per-op
- [ ] Billing telemetry: provisional vs final matches sample app expectations

Edge cases / open questions (TODOs):
- How to handle long-running streaming responses when device is offline? (Option: local stub + server attaches full stream on reconnection).
- Should SDK implement CRDT/text-merge for edit-heavy workflows? (trade-off: complexity vs UX)
- Data retention policy for offline caches (policy needed for Private deployments).
- Telemetry privacy controls: opt-in vs opt-out per region (GDPR/CCPA implications).

Observability / debug tooling (for developer-support):
- UI: offline sync status indicator (+ logs).
- SDK: expose debug dump of local DB (encrypted) for support upload.
- Server: provide reconciliation endpoint to replay ops and show divergence.

MVP scope (proposal): 6 weeks to first internal beta
- Week 1–2: prototype local store + enqueue/ack flow, basic syncAgent
- Week 3: server-side minimal /v1/offline/sync endpoint + token accounting
- Week 4: integrate token reconciliation and basic telemetry
- Week 5: mobile sample app, test matrix for connectivity patterns
- Week 6: beta release + docs + quickstart + support runbook

Notes to self / next steps:
- Pair with infra to stub an internal test end-to-end environment (low effort variant for dev keys). (Ravi)
- Wire up telemetry to cost dashboard so provisional vs final is visible in Console (Maya)
- Draft a small sample app for Android + iOS demonstrating a receipts summarizer with offline queue (Eli)

References / links:
- GH PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/678
- Related Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-Page-12345
- Tracking ticket: JIRA-ENG-904

Unresolved: rollout plan for Dedicated/Private customers who require strict data-at-rest retention. Need legal + security input.

-- end of draft --
